newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Nervy PGMs call shots in precious metals.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Nervy PGMs call shots in precious metals.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30

Platinum group metals (PGM) are under pressure after Russian officials arrived in Tokyo at the weekend for talks with Japanese customers, analysts said. But a one-day general strike call in South Africa may lend psychological support.
Gold is expected to trade quietly in a $341-$347 band.
PLATINUM - Bearish news that Russian and Japanese officials have launched supply talks is being balanced by a major strike action involving one-fifth of South Africa's miners, traders said.
"South Africa is the world's biggest platinum producer and this strike is going to be supportive even though the Russian-Japanese talks have started," a bullion dealer said.
The $400 an ounce level is psychological support for now, but the market is prone to severe volatility, he added.
At 0915 GMT spot platinum was quoted at $404.00/$407.00 an ounce, up $2.50 from Friday's New York close.
GOLD - The $341-$347 price range which has contained gold in recent weeks is likely to persist for now as the market closely watches the vulnerable PGMs for direction.
The drama being played out in Germany over revaluation of gold reserves, and developments in Europe over EMU criteria are also being closely watched.
But the market is also wary that Australian producers may start selling forward to take advantage of the higher Australian dollar gold price.
"We are starting to see interest from Australian producers -- it's time for them to start hedging," a dealer said.
AT 0815 GMT spot gold was indicated at $344.00/$345.00, little changed from Friday's New York close.
SILVER - Seen steady near term in a broad $4.60-$4.85 range as the focus remains firmly on the PGMs and gold.
At 0815 GMT spot silver was quoted at $4.73/$4.75, up three cents from Friday's New York close.
